subject.title: Bug: Poe image/video-output models are accepted in config but fail at runtime (Nano Banana 400, Veo/Sora fallback)

question: Should OpenClaw reject non-text-output models when configured as chat/session models, or add first-class output-modality metadata and runtime support for image/video outputs?
rationale: Both paths are plausible, but the choice changes public config semantics, provider ownership, model selection, and channel delivery behavior, so automation should not choose it from source inspection alone.

options.title: Reject Unsupported Chat Output
options.body: Add a clear diagnostic for image/video-output models selected as chat/session models and direct users to `image_generate` or `video_generate` until first-class support exists.

options.title: Add Output-Modality Support
options.body: Extend config/catalog metadata plus runtime/channel rendering so selected models can intentionally produce image/video outputs in session flow.

options.title: Docs-Only Clarification
options.body: Document that media generation must use generation tools while leaving current custom-provider behavior unchanged and accepting continued runtime confusion.

recommendation.title: Reject Unsupported Chat Output
recommendation.body: Add a clear diagnostic for image/video-output models selected as chat/session models and direct users to `image_generate` or `video_generate` until first-class support exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses provider/model config, docs, and media-generation direction where current and recent history show repeated ownership.
